11.note: The as much ... than clash could equally be fixed by changing the unmarked than to as; the marked segment still carries the error, accepted.

17.note: Key accepted, but it is the weakest item: wishes ... had flown in about a Saturday recital can be read as an acceptable past-perfect wish (they would have had to arrive already). If that reading holds, no segment is wrong. Recommend could fly in / would fly in framing be made unambiguous (e.g. recital is tomorrow vs. wish about a future arrival).

29.reason: Key is right (lets ... book), but the sentence is about an airport app and then says travelers arrive at the station. A careful student can reasonably pick that segment as the wrong word (should be airport). Also a self-consistency slip in the source.
